title: From video upload to HLS playback
description: A writing trial using an excerpt from the stream-app article: Spring Boot, S3, and an event-driven video pipeline.

children.text: Uploading a video file is easy. Turning that upload into a streamable asset — tracking state across services, deduplicating by content hash, transcoding to a browser-friendly format, and serving it securely — is where things get interesting.
The platform has three cooperating flows: upload, transcode, and playback.

body.alt: Stream-app architecture showing upload, transcode, and playback flows.
body.caption: The upload, transcoding, and playback flows in stream-app.

cells: Raw client upload via presigned PUT

body.title: A presigned manifest is not enough
body.text: A single presigned manifest URL does not authorize relative segment fetches from a private bucket. Production playback needs an access strategy such as CloudFront signed cookies or a media proxy.
